newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium praises Zaire talks, urges democracy.
newsitem.headline: Belgium praises Zaire talks, urges democracy.

text.p: Belgium on Monday welcomed a delayed weekend meeting between Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, and called for a peaceful end to the crisis in the country.

At Sunday's meeting Mobutu and Kabila -- whose rebel troops control most of the vast country and are said to be within days of entering the capital -- disagreed on arrangements for Mobutu to step down but agreed to meet again within 10 days.

"The Belgian government wishes to recall at this stage the importance that it attaches to a transition that takes account of the desires of the Zairean people and in which each Zairean will be allowed to participate in electing a democratic government," the Belgian foreign ministry said in a statement.

Belgium, the former colonial power in what is now Zaire, praised the diplomacy that made possible the meeting on board a South African naval vessel. It said it would support the Zairean electoral process in concert with the United Nations and the European Union.
The ministry said Belgium would cooperate with aid agencies to help relieve the suffering of thousands of refugees in east Zaire.
